weeks.title: Sounds of English
weeks.summary: English mein spelling aur sound hamesha same nahi hote. Is week aap vowels, consonants, silent letters aur -ed / -s endings ki pronunciation samjhoge.
concepts: **Letters vs sounds**: English mein sirf 26 letters hain, lekin standard British English mein lagbhag 44 sounds hain. Isliye spelling dekh kar pronunciation guess karna risky hai.
**Vowel sounds**: Letters a, e, i, o, u sirf 5 hain, par vowel sounds kaafi zyada hain (short, long aur diphthongs jaise 'ai' in 'time', 'oi' in 'boy').
**Consonant sounds**: p, b, t, d, k, g, f, v, s, z jaise sounds. Kuch sounds do letters se bante hain, jaise 'sh' in ship, 'ch' in chair, 'th' in think.
**Voiced vs voiceless**: Gale par haath rakh kar bolo. 'v' aur 'z' bolte waqt vibration hota hai (voiced), 'f' aur 's' mein nahi hota (voiceless). Pairs: p/b, t/d, f/v, s/z.
**Silent letters**: Kuch letters likhe jaate hain par bole nahi jaate: k in knee, h in honest, b in comb, t in listen, p in psychology.
**-ed ending ke 3 sounds**: Voiceless sound ke baad 't' (walked), voiced sound ke baad 'd' (played), aur t/d ke baad extra syllable 'id' (wanted, needed).
**-s / -es ending ke 3 sounds**: Voiceless ke baad 's' (cats), voiced ke baad 'z' (dogs), aur s, z, sh, ch ke baad extra syllable 'iz' (buses, watches).
**Vowel sound vs vowel letter**: 'university' u se shuru hota hai par sound 'yoo' (consonant sound) hai. 'hour' h se shuru hota hai par h silent hai, isliye vowel sound se shuru hota hai.

example.problem: Batao in teen words ka -ed kaise bolenge: walked, played, wanted.
steps: Pehle -ed se pehle wala last sound dekho, spelling nahi.
walked: 'k' voiceless sound hai, toh -ed ka sound 't' hoga: 'walkt'. Extra syllable nahi banta.
played: 'y/ay' voiced sound hai, toh -ed ka sound 'd' hoga: 'playd'.
wanted: last sound 't' hai, toh -ed ek naya syllable 'id' banata hai: 'wan-tid'.
Answer: walked = t, played = d, wanted = id (extra syllable).

mistakes: Har -ed ko 'id' bolna (jaise 'walk-id'). Yaad rakho: extra syllable sirf t ya d ke baad aata hai.
Silent letters bol dena, jaise 'k-nife' ya 'h-onest'. Naye words ki pronunciation dictionary mein sun kar check karo.
revision: 26 letters, lagbhag 44 sounds: spelling par blindly bharosa mat karo.
Voiced (vibration) vs voiceless (no vibration): b/p, d/t, v/f, z/s.
-ed: t (walked), d (played), id (wanted).
-s: s (cats), z (dogs), iz (buses).
Common silent letters: knee, honest, comb, listen, psychology.

questions.question: Which word has a silent 'k'?
questions.explanation: 'knee' mein k silent hai, word 'nee' jaisa bola jaata hai. kite, kick aur bake mein k clearly bola jaata hai.

questions.question: In which word is the letter 'h' silent?
questions.explanation: 'honour' mein h silent hai, word vowel sound 'o' se shuru hota hai, isliye 'an honour' bolte hain. hotel mein aaj ke standard English mein h bola jaata hai, wahi common trap hai.

questions.question: How is the '-ed' in 'wanted' pronounced?
questions.explanation: 'want' ka last sound t hai, aur t ya d ke baad -ed ek extra syllable 'id' banata hai: wan-tid. 't' sound walked jaise words mein aata hai, jahan pehle voiceless sound ho.

questions.question: In which word is the final '-s' pronounced like 'z'?
questions.explanation: 'dog' ka last sound g voiced hai, isliye -s ka sound 'z' hota hai: 'dogz'. cats, books, maps mein pehle t, k, p voiceless hain, isliye wahan -s ka sound 's' hi rehta hai.

questions.question: Which pair of words differs ONLY in voicing (one first sound is voiced, the other voiceless, made in the same way)?
questions.explanation: f aur v dono upper teeth aur lower lip se bante hain; farq sirf itna hai ki v mein gale mein vibration hai. fan/pan mein f aur p dono voiceless hain, sip/ship mein s aur sh dono voiceless hain, bat/mat mein b aur m dono voiced hain.

questions.question: Which word does NOT begin with a vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'university' u letter se shuru hota hai par sound 'yoo' hai, jo consonant sound hai, isliye 'a university'. hour aur honest mein h silent hai (vowel sound), aur umbrella 'uh' vowel sound se shuru hota hai. Trap: letter dekh kar answer mat do, sound suno.

weeks.title: Syllables and Word Stress
weeks.summary: Har English word ka ek syllable baaki se zyada zor se bola jaata hai. Is week aap syllables ginna, stress pehchanna aur noun-verb stress shift samjhoge.
concepts: **Syllable**: Word ka woh chhota hissa jismein ek vowel sound ho. 'wa-ter' = 2, 'ba-na-na' = 3, 'com-pu-ter' = 3 syllables.
**Word stress**: Stressed syllable thoda louder, lamba aur clear bola jaata hai. Jaise TA-ble, a-BOUT, be-GIN. Galat stress se word samajhna mushkil ho jaata hai.
**Two-syllable nouns vs verbs**: Zyadatar 2-syllable nouns aur adjectives mein stress 1st syllable par (DOC-tor, HAP-py), aur kai verbs mein 2nd par (be-GIN, de-CIDE, re-LAX).
**Noun-verb stress shift**: Same spelling, alag stress: REC-ord (noun) vs re-CORD (verb), PRES-ent (noun) vs pre-SENT (verb), OB-ject vs ob-JECT, PER-mit vs per-MIT.
**Suffix rules**: -tion, -sion, -ic, -ity se pehle wale syllable par stress: ed-u-CA-tion, de-CI-sion, sci-en-TIF-ic, a-BIL-i-ty.
**-graphy / -logy words**: Stress end se teesre syllable par: pho-TOG-ra-phy, bi-OL-o-gy. Compare: PHO-to-graph (stress 1st par).
**Compound nouns**: Do words se bane nouns mein usually stress pehle part par: BLACK-board, BED-room, CLASS-room.
**Weak sound (schwa)**: Unstressed syllables aksar halki 'uh' sound ban jaate hain, jaise 'a' in a-BOUT ya '-er' in TEACH-er.

example.problem: Is sentence mein 'record' ka stress batao: 'She wants to record a song that could set a world record.'
steps: Pehle dekho har 'record' sentence mein kya kaam kar raha hai.
'to record a song' mein record ek action hai, yaani verb.
Verb hai, toh stress 2nd syllable par: re-CORD.
'a world record' mein record ek cheez hai, yaani noun.
Noun hai, toh stress 1st syllable par: REC-ord.
Answer: pehla = re-CORD (verb), doosra = REC-ord (noun).

mistakes: Har word ke saare syllables ko barabar zor se bolna. English mein ek syllable clearly strong aur baaki halke hone chahiye.
Noun aur verb dono mein same stress lagana (jaise 'I will PRES-ent the award'). Pehle part of speech pehchano, phir stress lagao.
revision: Syllable = ek vowel sound wala chunk.
2-syllable noun: stress 1st (TA-ble); 2-syllable verb: aksar 2nd (be-GIN).
REC-ord / re-CORD, PRES-ent / pre-SENT: noun pehle, verb baad mein.
-tion, -ic, -ity: stress just pehle wale syllable par.
-graphy, -logy: pho-TOG-ra-phy, bi-OL-o-gy.

questions.question: How many syllables are there in the word 'computer'?
questions.explanation: com-pu-ter: teen vowel sounds, isliye 3 syllables. Letters ya vowels ki ginti mat karo, sirf bolte waqt alag-alag vowel sounds gino.

questions.question: In 'The principal will present the prizes', where is the stress on 'present'?
questions.explanation: Yahan 'present' ek action (verb) hai, matlab 'dena', isliye stress 2nd syllable par: pre-SENT. PRES-ent tab hota hai jab woh noun (gift) ya adjective ho.

questions.question: Which word is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: be-GIN ek 2-syllable verb hai jiska stress 2nd syllable par hai. DOC-tor, HAP-py aur WIN-dow sab 1st syllable par stressed hain.

questions.question: The word 'photography' has four syllables: pho-tog-ra-phy. Which syllable is stressed?
questions.explanation: -graphy wale words mein stress end se teesre syllable par aata hai, isliye pho-TOG-ra-phy (2nd syllable). Trap: 'PHO-to-graph' mein stress 1st par hai, isliye students wahi pattern yahan bhi laga dete hain.

questions.question: The word 'education' has four syllables: ed-u-ca-tion. Which syllable is stressed?
questions.explanation: -tion se just pehle wale syllable par stress aata hai, isliye ed-u-CA-tion (3rd syllable). -tion khud kabhi stressed nahi hota, woh halka 'shun' bola jaata hai.

questions.question: In which sentence is the word in quotes stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: 'a lovely present' mein present ek noun (gift) hai, isliye PRES-ent. Baaki teeno (object, record, permit) yahan verbs hain, isliye unka stress 2nd syllable par hai: ob-JECT, re-CORD, per-MIT.

weeks.title: Parts of Speech
weeks.summary: Har word sentence mein koi kaam karta hai: naam batana, action batana, describe karna ya jodna. Is week aap 8 parts of speech aur 'kaam se pehchan' ka rule seekhoge.
concepts: **Noun**: Kisi person, place, thing ya idea ka naam: Priya, Delhi, laptop, honesty.
**Pronoun**: Noun ki jagah use hota hai taaki repeat na karna pade: he, she, it, they, them, this, who.
**Verb**: Action ya state batata hai: run, write, is, seem, become.
**Adjective**: Noun ya pronoun ko describe karta hai: tall boy, red pen, three books, she is tired.
**Adverb**: Verb, adjective ya doosre adverb ko modify karta hai; kaise, kab, kahan, kitna: runs quickly, very tall, came yesterday.

**Preposition aur Conjunction**: Preposition noun/pronoun ka relation batata hai (in, on, under, after the class). Conjunction words ya clauses ko jodta hai (and, but, because, until the rain stopped).
**Interjection**: Achanak feeling dikhane wala word: Oh! Wow! Ouch!
**Kaam se pehchan**: Ek hi word alag sentences mein alag part of speech ho sakta hai. 'fast' = adjective (a fast car), adverb (he runs fast), verb (they fast on Monday).

example.problem: Is sentence ke har word ka part of speech batao: 'Wow, the new student answered very confidently.'
steps: Wow: feeling dikha raha hai, toh interjection.
the: noun 'student' se pehle article (determiner, adjective jaisa kaam).
new: student ko describe kar raha hai, toh adjective.
student: person ka naam, toh noun.
answered: action, toh verb.
very: 'confidently' ko modify kar raha hai, toh adverb.
confidently: batata hai kaise answer kiya, toh adverb.
Answer: Wow (interjection), the (article), new (adjective), student (noun), answered (verb), very (adverb), confidently (adverb).

mistakes: Word ko ratta maar ke ek hi category dena. Hamesha dekho sentence mein woh kya kaam kar raha hai.
Har -ly word ko adverb maan lena. 'friendly', 'lovely', 'lonely' adjectives hain: 'a friendly teacher'.
revision: Noun = naam, Pronoun = noun ki jagah, Verb = action/state.
Adjective noun ko describe karta hai, adverb verb/adjective/adverb ko.
Preposition + noun (after lunch); conjunction + clause (after we had lunch).
Part of speech word ke kaam se decide hota hai, spelling se nahi.

questions.question: In 'She sings beautifully', the word 'beautifully' is:
questions.explanation: 'beautifully' batata hai ki woh kaise gaati hai, yaani verb 'sings' ko modify kar raha hai, isliye adverb. 'beautiful' (bina -ly) adjective hota, jaise 'a beautiful song'.

questions.question: Which word is a pronoun in 'Ravi gave them a book'?
questions.explanation: 'them' kuch logon ke naam ki jagah use hua hai, isliye pronoun. Ravi aur book nouns hain, gave verb hai.

questions.question: In 'He works hard', the word 'hard' is:
questions.explanation: Yahan 'hard' batata hai ki woh kaise kaam karta hai, yaani verb 'works' ko modify kar raha hai, isliye adverb. Trap: 'a hard question' mein hard adjective hai, kyunki wahan noun ko describe kar raha hai.

questions.question: In 'We waited until the rain stopped', the word 'until' is:
questions.explanation: 'until' ke baad poora clause hai ('the rain stopped', jismein subject aur verb dono hain), isliye yahan woh conjunction hai. 'until Monday' jaise phrase mein (sirf noun) woh preposition hota.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in 'The tired children fell asleep early'?
questions.explanation: 'tired' noun 'children' ko describe kar raha hai, isliye adjective. 'early' yahan batata hai kab so gaye, yaani verb ko modify kar raha hai, isliye adverb hai.

questions.question: In which sentence is 'round' used as a preposition?
options: They will round the figure off to 50.
The earth goes round the sun.
questions.explanation: 'round the sun' mein round noun 'sun' ke saath relation (direction) bata raha hai, isliye preposition. 'a round face' mein adjective, 'the first round' mein noun, aur 'round the figure off' mein verb hai.

weeks.title: Tenses in Use
weeks.summary: Tense batata hai action kab hua aur kis tarah. Is week aap simple, continuous aur perfect tenses ka sahi use, aur common time-word traps seekhoge.
concepts: **12 tenses ka structure**: 3 times (present, past, future) x 4 aspects (simple, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous).
**Simple present**: Habits aur universal facts ke liye: 'She walks to college daily', 'The sun rises in the east'.
**Present continuous**: Abhi chal raha action ya temporary situation: 'Look, it is raining.'
**Present perfect**: Past ka action jiska connection present se ho, bina specific past time ke: 'I have finished my assignment.' since/for ke saath bhi: 'She has lived here since 2019.'
**Simple past**: Specific past time ke saath (yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago): 'I met him yesterday.' Yahan present perfect galat hai.
**Past perfect**: Past ke do actions mein jo pehle hua: 'The train had left before we reached.'
**Future**: 'will' instant decision ya prediction ke liye; 'be going to' pehle se bane plan ke liye: 'I am going to visit Jaipur next month.'
**Stative verbs**: know, believe, own, understand, like jaise state verbs normally continuous mein nahi aate: 'I know the answer', na ki 'I am knowing'.

example.problem: Sentence sahi karo: 'I have completed the project last Monday.'
steps: Time expression dhoondo: 'last Monday'. Yeh ek specific, finished past time hai.
Rule: specific past time ke saath present perfect (have + V3) nahi lagta.
Isliye simple past use karo: completed.
Answer: 'I completed the project last Monday.'

mistakes: Present perfect ko yesterday, last year, ago jaise words ke saath use karna. In words ke saath simple past lagao.
Stative verbs ko -ing form mein likhna: 'I am having two brothers' galat hai, sahi hai 'I have two brothers'.
revision: Habit/fact = simple present; abhi = present continuous.
Specific past time = simple past (yesterday, ago, last week).
Present connection, no fixed time = present perfect (have/has + V3).
Do past actions mein pehla = past perfect (had + V3).
know, own, believe, understand: continuous mein mat lagao.

questions.question: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: Yeh ek scientific fact hai jo hamesha sach hai, isliye simple present 'boils'. 'is boiling' tab hota jab koi specific paani abhi ubal raha ho.

questions.question: Look! The baby ___.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' batata hai ki action abhi is waqt ho raha hai, isliye present continuous 'is sleeping'. 'sleeps' habit ke liye hota hai, abhi ke action ke liye nahi.

questions.question: I ___ him at the library yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'yesterday' ek specific finished past time hai, isliye simple past 'met'. Sabse common trap 'have met' hai, par present perfect specific past time ke saath nahi aata.

questions.question: She ___ in Chennai since 2019.
questions.explanation: 'since 2019' batata hai ki action past mein shuru hua aur abhi tak chal raha hai, isliye present perfect 'has lived'. 'lives' ya 'is living' ke saath since nahi lagta.

questions.question: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: Do past actions hain: train ka jaana pehle hua, humara pahunchna baad mein. Pehle wale action ke liye past perfect 'had left'. 'By the time' wale sentences mein yeh pattern bahut common hai.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct in standard English?
options: I have finished the work yesterday.
I am understanding your point now.
She has been owning this car for years.
He has lived here since he was a child.
questions.explanation: 'has lived ... since' present perfect ka sahi use hai. Option 1 mein 'yesterday' ke saath present perfect galat hai. Options 2 aur 3 mein stative verbs (understand, own) ko continuous mein use kiya hai, jo standard academic English mein galat maana jaata hai.

weeks.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
weeks.summary: Singular subject ke saath singular verb, plural ke saath plural. Is week aap each, neither-nor, along with, a number of jaise tricky cases seekhoge.
concepts: **Basic rule**: Singular subject + singular verb (She **writes**), plural subject + plural verb (They **write**). Present tense mein singular verb par -s/-es lagta hai.
**Each / every / everyone**: Yeh hamesha singular verb lete hain: 'Each of the students **has** a laptop', 'Everyone **is** here'.
**Either...or / Neither...nor**: Verb nazdeek wale (second) subject se match karta hai: 'Neither the teacher nor the students **were** ready.'
**Along with / as well as / together with**: Verb pehle (main) subject se match karta hai: 'The captain, along with his players, **has** arrived.'
**A number of vs The number of**: 'A number of students **are** absent' (bahut saare = plural). 'The number of students **is** 50' (ginti = singular).
**One of the + plural noun**: Subject 'one' hai, isliye verb singular: 'One of my friends **lives** in Canada.'
**Uncountable nouns**: news, information, advice, furniture singular verb lete hain: 'The news **is** good.'
**Collective nouns**: team, family, class jab ek unit ki tarah act karein toh singular: 'The team **is** playing well.'

example.problem: Sentence sahi karo: 'The list of items are on the table.'
steps: Asli subject dhoondo. 'of items' sirf ek extra phrase hai.
Main subject 'The list' hai, jo singular hai.
Singular subject ke saath singular verb: 'is'.
Verb ke paas wale noun 'items' se confuse mat ho.
Answer: 'The list of items is on the table.'

mistakes: Verb ko paas wale noun se match karna (jaise 'The box of pens are...'). Hamesha asli subject dhoondo aur 'of ...' wala phrase hata ke dekho.
'news', 'information', 'advice' ko plural treat karna ya inke saath 's' lagana ('informations'). Yeh uncountable aur singular hain.
revision: each, every, everyone = singular verb.
either/or, neither/nor: verb paas wale subject se match karta hai.
along with, as well as: verb pehle subject se match karta hai.
A number of = plural; The number of = singular.
One of the + plural noun + singular verb.

questions.question: Each of the students ___ a laptop.
questions.explanation: Subject 'Each' hai, jo hamesha singular hota hai, isliye 'has'. Trap: 'students' plural hai par woh 'of' phrase ke andar hai, asli subject nahi.

questions.question: The news ___ good today.
questions.explanation: 'news' ke end mein s hai par yeh uncountable aur singular noun hai, isliye 'is'. Spelling dekh kar plural mat samjho.

questions.question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready for the test.
questions.explanation: Neither...nor mein verb nazdeek wale subject se match karta hai. Yahan nazdeek 'the students' (plural) hai, isliye 'were'. 'was' tab sahi hota jab order ulta hota: 'Neither the students nor the teacher was ready.'

questions.question: The captain, along with his players, ___ arrived at the ground.
questions.explanation: 'along with his players' extra information hai; main subject 'The captain' singular hai, isliye 'has'. Trap: 'players' paas hone ki wajah se log 'have' chun lete hain.

questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' ka matlab hai 'bahut saare', isliye plural verb 'are'. 'The number of students is...' mein singular hota, kyunki wahan baat ek ginti (number) ki hoti hai.

questions.question: One of my friends ___ in Canada.
questions.explanation: Asli subject 'One' hai, 'friends' nahi, isliye singular verb 'lives'. 'One of + plural noun' ka pattern yaad rakho: noun plural, verb singular.

weeks.title: Articles and Determiners
weeks.summary: a, an, the aur some, many, much, few jaise words noun se pehle aate hain. Is week aap a/an ka sound wala rule, 'the' ka use aur quantifiers ka sahi choice seekhoge.
concepts: **A vs An**: Choice sound par depend karta hai, letter par nahi. Vowel sound se pehle 'an' (an apple, an hour, an MBA), consonant sound se pehle 'a' (a university, a one-day match, a European).

**The**: Specific ya pehle mention ki hui cheez ke liye (I bought a pen. **The** pen is blue.), unique cheezon ke liye (the sun, the internet), aur rivers, oceans ke naam ke saath (the Ganga, the Indian Ocean).
**The with superlatives and ordinals**: the best, the tallest, the first, the second.
**The with musical instruments**: 'She plays **the** guitar.' (Sports ke saath nahi: 'He plays cricket.')
**Zero article**: General plural ya uncountable nouns, abstract ideas aur meals ke saath article nahi: 'Milk is healthy', 'Honesty is important', 'We had lunch'.
**Demonstratives**: this/that (singular), these/those (plural): 'this book', 'those chairs'.
**Many vs Much**: many countable plural ke saath (many books), much uncountable ke saath (much water), aksar negative aur questions mein.
**Few vs A few, Little vs A little**: 'a few / a little' = thoda, kaafi hai (positive). 'few / little' = bahut kam, lagbhag nahi (negative).

example.problem: Blanks bharo: 'She is ___ honest girl. She wants to join ___ university in ___ USA.'
steps: 'honest' mein h silent hai, sound vowel 'o' se shuru hota hai, isliye 'an honest girl'.
'university' ka sound 'yoo' se shuru hota hai (consonant sound), isliye 'a university'.
'USA' ek aisa country naam hai jismein 'States' plural hai, isliye 'the USA'. Iska pehla sound 'yoo' hai, par yahan 'the' hi lagta hai.
Answer: 'She is an honest girl. She wants to join a university in the USA.'

mistakes: a/an ko letter dekh kar choose karna ('an university', 'a hour'). Word bol kar dekho, pehla sound kya hai.
Abstract nouns aur meals se pehle 'the' lagana ('The honesty is best policy', 'I had a breakfast'). General meaning mein article hatao.
revision: a/an = sound ke hisaab se: an hour, a university.
the = specific, unique, rivers, superlatives, instruments.
General plural/uncountable/abstract/meals = no article.
many + countable, much + uncountable.
a few = kuch (positive), few = bahut kam (negative).

questions.question: She is ___ honest person.
questions.explanation: 'honest' mein h silent hai, word vowel sound 'o' se shuru hota hai, isliye 'an'. Letter h dekh kar 'a' lagana sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: There isn't ___ milk left in the fridge.
questions.explanation: 'milk' uncountable noun hai, aur negative sentence hai, isliye 'much'. many, few, a few sirf countable plural nouns (books, students) ke saath aate hain.

questions.question: Which phrase is correct?
questions.explanation: 'European' ka pehla sound 'yoo' hai (consonant sound), isliye 'a European'. 'an university' (yoo sound), 'a hour' (h silent, vowel sound) aur 'an one-day' (w sound) teeno galat hain.

questions.question: ___ Ganga is a holy river for many Indians.
questions.explanation: Rivers ke naam se pehle 'the' lagta hai: the Ganga, the Yamuna, the Nile. Cities aur countries (jaise Delhi, India) ke saath article nahi lagta, wahi confusion ka source hai.

questions.question: I have ___ good friends here, so I don't feel lonely.
questions.explanation: 'friends' countable hai aur sentence positive meaning de raha hai (lonely nahi lagta), isliye 'a few'. 'few' ka matlab 'bahut kam, lagbhag nahi' hota, jo 'I don't feel lonely' se match nahi karta. little/a little uncountable ke liye hain.

questions.question: Which sentence uses articles correctly?
options: The honesty is the best policy.
She plays the piano every evening.
He is best player in the team.
I had a breakfast at eight.
questions.explanation: Musical instruments ke saath 'the' lagta hai: 'plays the piano'. Option 1 mein abstract noun 'honesty' general sense mein hai, 'the' nahi lagega. Option 3 mein superlative 'best' se pehle 'the' missing hai. Option 4 mein simple meal 'breakfast' se pehle 'a' nahi lagta.

weeks.title: Prepositions
weeks.summary: Chhote words jaise in, on, at, since, for bahut galtiyan karwaate hain. Is week aap time aur place prepositions, since vs for, aur fixed verb + preposition combinations seekhoge.
concepts: **Time: at / on / in**: at exact time (at 9 a.m., at night), on days aur dates (on Monday, on 15 August), in months, years, seasons, parts of day (in July, in 2024, in the morning).
**Place: at / on / in**: at ek point (at the bus stop), on surface (on the table), in andar (in the room, in Mumbai).
**Since vs For**: since ke baad starting point (since 2020, since Monday), for ke baad duration (for two hours, for three years).
**Between vs Among**: between do clearly alag cheezon ke beech, among ek group ke beech: 'among all the students'.
**By vs With**: by transport/agent ke liye (by bus, written by Premchand), with tool ke liye (write with a pen).
**Fixed combinations**: good at, interested in, depend on, afraid of, married to, angry with (person). Inhe phrase ki tarah yaad karo.
**No preposition after some verbs**: discuss, enter, reach, attend, ask ke baad direct object aata hai: 'discuss the plan', 'reach the station' (na ki 'discuss about', 'reach at').

example.problem: Sentence sahi karo: 'I am living in Pune since three years and we discussed about it on the morning.'
steps: 'three years' ek duration hai, starting point nahi, isliye 'since' ki jagah 'for'.
Past se abhi tak chal rahi situation hai, toh present perfect better hai: 'I have lived in Pune for three years.'
'discuss' ke baad preposition nahi lagta: 'discussed it'.
Parts of the day ke saath 'in' lagta hai: 'in the morning'.
Answer: 'I have lived in Pune for three years, and we discussed it in the morning.'

mistakes: 'since' ko duration ke saath use karna ('since two hours'). Duration = for, starting point = since.
Hindi ke 'ke baare mein' ki wajah se 'discuss about' likhna. discuss ke baad seedha object aata hai.
revision: at 5 p.m. / on Monday / in July.
at the gate / on the desk / in the bag.
since + point in time; for + duration.
good at, interested in, depend on, afraid of.
discuss, reach, enter, attend: koi preposition nahi.

questions.question: The class starts ___ 9 a.m.
questions.explanation: Exact clock time ke saath 'at' lagta hai: at 9 a.m. 'on' days/dates ke liye aur 'in' months/years ke liye hota hai.

questions.question: My birthday is ___ 15 August.
questions.explanation: Specific date ke saath 'on' lagta hai: on 15 August. 'in August' sahi hota agar sirf mahina hota, par date ke saath 'on' hi aata hai.

questions.question: I have been waiting ___ two hours.
questions.explanation: 'two hours' ek duration (kitni der) hai, isliye 'for'. 'since' sirf starting point ke saath aata hai, jaise 'since 4 p.m.'.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: We discussed regarding about the plan.
questions.explanation: 'discuss' ke baad seedha object aata hai, koi preposition nahi: 'discussed the plan'. 'discussed about' Hindi ke 'ke baare mein' se aane wali common galti hai. (Noun ke saath 'a discussion about' sahi hai.)

questions.question: The teacher divided the sweets ___ all the students in the class.
questions.explanation: Poori class ek group hai, isliye 'among'. 'between' do (ya clearly alag-alag naam liye gaye) logon ke liye hota hai.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the preposition correctly?
options: They reached at the station late.
questions.explanation: 'depend on' sahi fixed combination hai. Baaki teen galat hain: 'good at mathematics', 'interested in music', aur 'reached the station' (reach ke baad 'at' nahi lagta).

weeks.title: Sentence Types and Structure
weeks.summary: Sentences kaam ke hisaab se (statement, question, order, exclamation) aur structure ke hisaab se (simple, compound, complex) alag hote hain. Is week aap inhe pehchanna aur run-on galtiyan theek karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Declarative**: Statement deta hai, full stop se khatam: 'The lecture starts at 6.'
**Interrogative**: Sawaal poochta hai; auxiliary subject se pehle: 'Are you ready?', 'What does she study?'
**Imperative**: Order, request ya instruction; subject 'you' hidden hota hai: 'Please close the door.'
**Exclamatory**: Strong feeling: 'What a beautiful view this is!', 'How fast she runs!'
**Simple vs Compound**: Simple = ek independent clause. Compound = do independent clauses jo for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so (FANBOYS) se jude hon: 'I studied, but I was tired.'
**Complex**: Ek independent clause + ek dependent clause (because, although, when, if, which ke saath): 'Although she was tired, she finished the work.'
**Indirect questions**: 'Can you tell me...' ke baad normal statement order: 'Can you tell me where the bank is?' (na ki 'where is the bank').
**Run-on aur comma splice**: Do complete sentences ko sirf comma se ya bina kisi punctuation ke jodna galat hai. Full stop, semicolon ya conjunction use karo.

example.problem: Is galat sentence ko teen sahi tarikon se likho: 'It was raining, we stayed inside.'
steps: Do independent clauses hain: 'It was raining' aur 'we stayed inside'. Sirf comma se jodna comma splice hai.
Tarika 1 (full stop): 'It was raining. We stayed inside.'
Tarika 2 (comma + FANBOYS, compound): 'It was raining, so we stayed inside.'
Tarika 3 (dependent clause, complex): 'Because it was raining, we stayed inside.'
Answer: teeno version sahi hain; galat sirf original comma splice tha.

mistakes: Indirect question mein bhi question order rakhna ('Tell me what is your name'). Sahi: 'Tell me what your name is.'
'Because it was late.' jaise dependent clause ko akele full sentence maan lena. Yeh fragment hai; ise main clause se jodo.
revision: 4 functional types: declarative, interrogative, imperative, exclamatory.
Compound = 2 independent clauses + FANBOYS.
Complex = independent + dependent clause (because, although, when).
Indirect question = statement order: where the bank is.
Comma splice theek karne ke liye: full stop, semicolon ya conjunction.

questions.question: What type of sentence is 'Please close the door.'?
questions.explanation: Yeh ek request/instruction hai jismein subject 'you' hidden hai, isliye imperative. Full stop dekh kar declarative mat samjho; declarative sirf information deta hai.

questions.question: What type of sentence is 'What a beautiful view this is!'?
questions.explanation: Yeh strong feeling (surprise/admiration) dikhata hai aur 'What a ...!' pattern mein hai, isliye exclamatory. 'What' se shuru hone par bhi yeh question nahi hai, kyunki word order statement wala hai aur end mein '!' hai.

questions.question: 'I wanted to go out, but it was raining.' This sentence is:
questions.explanation: Do independent clauses ('I wanted to go out' aur 'it was raining') coordinating conjunction 'but' se jude hain, isliye compound. Complex tab hota jab ek clause dependent hota (jaise because/although se shuru).

questions.question: 'Although she was tired, she finished the assignment.' This sentence is:
questions.explanation: 'Although she was tired' dependent clause hai (akele complete nahi), aur 'she finished the assignment' independent clause hai. Dependent + independent = complex sentence.

questions.question: Which is a correctly formed indirect question?
options: Can you tell me where is the bank?
Can you tell me where does the bank is?
Can you tell me the bank where is?
Can you tell me where the bank is?
questions.explanation: 'Can you tell me' ke baad wala hissa statement order mein aata hai: subject (the bank) + verb (is). 'where is the bank' direct question ka order hai, jo yahan galat hai.

questions.question: Which option is correctly punctuated?
options: The exam was easy, I finished early.
The exam was easy I finished early.
The exam was easy; I finished early.
questions.explanation: Semicolon do closely related independent clauses ko sahi tarike se jodta hai. Option 1 comma splice hai, option 2 run-on hai (koi punctuation nahi), aur option 4 fragment hai (sirf dependent clause).

weeks.title: Vocabulary Building
weeks.summary: Achhi vocabulary sirf naye words nahi, sahi word sahi jagah use karna hai. Is week aap synonyms, antonyms, collocations, phrasal verbs aur confusing word pairs seekhoge.
concepts: **Synonyms with shades**: Milte-julte words ka intensity alag hota hai: big < huge < enormous; happy < delighted < thrilled. Context ke hisaab se choose karo.
**Antonyms with prefixes**: un- (unhappy), in- (incorrect), im- (impossible, p/b/m se pehle), il- (illegal), ir- (irregular), dis- (dislike).
**Collocations**: Words jo natural tarike se saath aate hain: make a mistake, do homework, heavy rain, strong tea, pay attention. 'do a mistake' ya 'strong rain' unnatural lagta hai.
**Phrasal verbs**: Verb + particle se naya meaning: look after (care karna), give up (chhod dena), put off (postpone karna), run out of (khatam ho jaana), turn down (mana karna).
**Root words**: bio = life (biology), graph = write (autograph), port = carry (transport), pre- = before (preview), mis- = wrong (misunderstand).
**Confusing pairs**: affect (verb, asar daalna) vs effect (noun, asar); advice (noun) vs advise (verb); lose (khona) vs loose (dheela).
**Context clues**: Anjaan word ka meaning aas-paas ke words se guess karo, jaise examples, contrast words (but, however) ya definition.

example.problem: Sahi words chuno: 'Please don't (do / make) noise. The doctor (adviced / advised) rest, and the medicine will (affect / effect) your sleep.'
steps: Collocation: noise ke saath 'make' aata hai, isliye 'make noise'.
advise verb hai, uska past 'advised' hai. 'adviced' koi word nahi hai.
'will' ke baad verb chahiye; asar daalna = affect (verb). effect usually noun hota hai.
Answer: 'Please don't make noise. The doctor advised rest, and the medicine will affect your sleep.'

mistakes: Hindi se seedha translate karna, jaise 'strong rain' (tez baarish). English collocation 'heavy rain' hai; examples padh kar natural pairs yaad karo.
Dictionary se synonym utha kar bina context ke use karna. Pehle example sentence dekho ki word formal hai ya informal, positive ya negative.
revision: Collocations: make a mistake, do homework, heavy rain, strong coffee.
Prefix antonyms: im-possible, ir-regular, il-legal, dis-agree.
Phrasal verbs: put off = postpone, give up = quit, look after = care for.
affect = verb, effect = noun (mostly).
Naye words context ke saath seekho, akele list mein nahi.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'rapid'.
questions.explanation: 'rapid' ka matlab hai bahut tez, isliye synonym 'quick'. 'slow' iska antonym hai, aur heavy/calm ka speed se direct relation nahi hai.

questions.question: Choose the correct opposite of 'possible'.
questions.explanation: 'p' se shuru hone wale words ke saath prefix 'in-' badal kar 'im-' ban jaata hai: impossible, impatient, impolite. Baaki teeno English words nahi hain.

questions.question: Please don't ___ a mistake while filling the form.
questions.explanation: Natural collocation 'make a mistake' hai. 'do a mistake' Indian English mein suna jaata hai par standard English mein galat maana jaata hai. 'do' ke saath homework, work, exercise aate hain.

questions.question: The meeting has been ___ till Friday because the manager is unwell.
questions.explanation: 'put off' = postpone karna, aage badha dena, jo yahan context se match karta hai. 'put on' = pehenna (put on a jacket), 'put out' = aag ya light bujhana.

questions.question: We had very ___ rain last night, and the roads were flooded.
questions.explanation: Rain ke saath natural collocation 'heavy rain' hai. 'strong rain' Hindi ke 'tez baarish' ka direct translation hai; 'strong' wind ya coffee ke saath aata hai, rain ke saath nahi.

questions.question: Lack of sleep can badly ___ your memory.
questions.explanation: 'can' ke baad base verb chahiye jiska matlab 'asar daalna' ho, isliye 'affect'. 'effect' mostly noun hai (a bad effect); 'effects' plural noun hai, aur 'affection' ka matlab pyaar hai.

weeks.title: Reading and Listening Skills
weeks.summary: Comprehension ka matlab hai text ya audio se sahi information nikalna. Is week aap skimming, scanning, main idea, context clues aur inference ke saath True/False/Not Given trap samjhoge.
concepts: **Skimming**: Text jaldi se padh kar overall idea (gist) samajhna. Pehli aur aakhri lines aur headings par dhyaan do.
**Scanning**: Kisi specific information (date, number, naam) ko dhoondna. Poora text dheere padhne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf keyword dhoondo.
**Main idea vs details**: Main idea poore paragraph ka central point hai; details use support karte hain. Ek chhoti detail ko main idea mat samjho.
**Signal words**: however/but = contrast, therefore/so = result, for example = example, moreover = addition, finally = sequence ka end.
**Context clues**: Anjaan word ka meaning aas-paas ke words se guess karo, jaise 'so cramped that people had to stand shoulder to shoulder'.
**Inference**: Jo directly likha nahi par text se logically nikalta hai. Inference text par based hona chahiye, apni imagination par nahi.
**True / False / Not Given**: True = text confirm karta hai, False = text contradict karta hai, Not Given = text mein is baare mein information hi nahi hai.
**Active listening**: Sunne se pehle question padho aur predict karo, keywords note karo, aur speaker ke stress aur pauses par dhyaan do.

example.problem: Text: 'The college canteen now closes at 8 p.m. instead of 9 p.m. However, students can still order snacks online until 10 p.m.' Statement: 'Students cannot get any snacks after 8 p.m.' Kya yeh True, False ya Not Given hai?
steps: Statement ka keyword: 'after 8 p.m.' aur 'cannot get any snacks'.
Text scan karo: canteen 8 p.m. par band hoti hai, yeh sach hai.
Signal word 'However' contrast dikha raha hai: online order 10 p.m. tak ho sakta hai.
Matlab 8 p.m. ke baad bhi snacks mil sakte hain, toh text statement ko contradict karta hai.
Answer: False.

mistakes: Apni general knowledge se answer dena. Comprehension mein sirf woh maano jo text mein likha hai ya usse clearly nikalta hai.
'False' aur 'Not Given' mein confuse hona. False tab hai jab text ulta kehta hai; Not Given tab jab text kuch bhi nahi kehta.
revision: Skim = gist; scan = specific fact.
Main idea = poore text ka central point.
however = contrast, therefore = result.
Inference text se nikalna chahiye, imagination se nahi.
Not Given = text mein information hi nahi hai.

questions.question: Notice: 'The library will stay open till 10 p.m. from Monday to Friday, and till 6 p.m. on Saturday. It remains closed on Sunday.' Till what time is the library open on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Scanning karo: 'Saturday' keyword ke saath '6 p.m.' likha hai. 10 p.m. weekdays ke liye hai, aur 'closed' Sunday ke liye, wahi traps hain.

questions.question: Read: 'Drinking enough water helps the body control its temperature. It also keeps joints moving smoothly and helps the kidneys remove waste.' What is the main idea?
options: Kidneys remove waste from the body.
Water helps the body in several ways.
questions.explanation: Poora text paani ke alag-alag fayde bata raha hai, isliye main idea 'Water helps the body in several ways'. Option 1 sirf ek supporting detail hai; options 3 aur 4 text mein hain hi nahi.

questions.question: Read: 'Arjun practised every day for a month. ___, he still felt nervous before the debate.' Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: Roz practice ke baad bhi nervous hona ek contrast hai (expected ke ulta), isliye 'However'. 'Therefore' result dikhata, jaise practice ki wajah se confident hona.

questions.question: Read: 'The hall was so cramped that people had to stand shoulder to shoulder, and some could not even get in.' Here, 'cramped' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Context clue: log kandhe se kandha mila kar khade the aur kuch andar bhi nahi aa paaye, matlab jagah kam aur bheed zyada thi. Isliye 'too small and crowded'.

questions.question: Read: 'Meera runs a tea stall near a college. She opens at 6 a.m. and offers a cheaper cup to students who bring their own steel tumbler.' Statement: 'Meera's stall is the only tea stall near the college.' This statement is:
questions.explanation: Text mein doosre tea stalls ke baare mein koi information nahi hai, na haan na naa. Isliye 'Not Given'. 'False' tab hota jab text kehta ki wahan aur stalls bhi hain.

questions.question: Read: 'When Meera started the offer, only a few students brought tumblers. By the end of the semester, almost half her customers were carrying them, and the road outside looked much cleaner.' Which inference is best supported by the text?
options: Most students refused the offer for the whole year.
Students' habits changed gradually over the semester.
Meera stopped using paper cups completely.
The college gave Meera an award for her idea.
questions.explanation: Shuru mein 'a few' aur end mein 'almost half' batata hai ki change dheere-dheere hua, isliye option 2 best supported hai. Option 1 text ke ulta hai, option 3 likha nahi (half customers hi tumbler laate the), aur option 4 ka koi mention nahi hai.

weeks.title: Introductions and Small Talk
weeks.summary: Kisi se pehli baar milna, apna introduction dena aur halki-phulki baat-cheet karna confidence ki skill hai. Is week aap formal/informal greetings, polite requests aur common Indian-English galtiyan seekhoge.
concepts: **Formal vs informal greetings**: Formal: 'Good morning', 'Nice to meet you'. Informal: 'Hi', 'Hey, how's it going?'. Setting dekh kar choose karo.
**Meet vs See**: 'Nice to meet you' pehli mulaqat par; 'Nice to see you (again)' kisi jaan-pehchaan wale se milne par.
**Self-introduction structure**: Greeting, naam, background (city/education), abhi kya kar rahe ho, ek interest, aur polite closing. 30-60 seconds kaafi hai.
**Polite requests**: 'Could you please...?', 'Would you mind...?' order jaisa nahi lagta. 'Give me' ya 'I want' rude lag sakta hai.
**Small talk topics**: Safe: weather, studies, course, events, hobbies, travel. Avoid: salary, age, religion, weight, politics, personal problems.
**Keeping a conversation going**: Short answer ke baad open follow-up question poocho: 'Oh nice! What's it like living there?'

**Avoid common Indianisms in formal speech**: 'Myself Rahul' ki jagah 'I'm Rahul'; 'I am having two brothers' ki jagah 'I have two brothers'; 'passed out from college' ki jagah 'graduated from college'.

example.problem: Is introduction ko improve karo: 'Myself Priya. I am belonging to Bhopal. I am having interest in data science.'
steps: 'Myself Priya' standard English nahi hai; likho 'I'm Priya' ya 'My name is Priya'.
'belong' stative verb hai, continuous mein nahi aata; aur 'from' zyada natural hai: 'I'm from Bhopal.'
'I am having interest' bhi stative verb ka galat use hai; likho 'I'm interested in data science.'
Greeting aur closing add karo taaki introduction complete lage.
Answer: 'Good morning! I'm Priya, and I'm from Bhopal. I'm interested in data science, and I'm excited to learn with all of you.'

mistakes: 'Myself ...' se introduction shuru karna. 'myself' reflexive pronoun hai; introduction mein 'I'm ...' ya 'My name is ...' bolo.
Small talk mein sirf 'Yes', 'Okay' bol kar baat khatam kar dena. Har jawab ke baad ek chhota follow-up question poocho.
revision: Pehli mulaqat: 'Nice to meet you'.
Introduction: greeting, naam, background, current, interest, closing.
Requests: 'Could you please...?'
Safe topics: studies, weather, hobbies; avoid salary, religion, age.
'Myself X' nahi, 'I'm X'.

questions.question: You meet someone for the first time at a seminar. What is the most appropriate thing to say?
questions.explanation: Pehli mulaqat par 'Nice to meet you' kehte hain. 'see you again' aur 'Long time no see' tab use hote hain jab aap pehle se jaante ho, aur 'What's up, buddy?' seminar ke liye bahut informal hai.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to ask a classmate for their notes?
options: Could you please lend me your notes?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...?' ek polite request ka standard pattern hai. Baaki options order jaise lagte hain aur rude sound kar sakte hain, bhale hi grammar sahi ho.

questions.question: Which topic is the safest for small talk with a new classmate?
options: How they found today's live session
questions.explanation: Course ya aaj ki class jaisa shared experience safe aur easy topic hai. Income, religion aur weight personal ya sensitive topics hain jo pehli baat-cheet mein avoid karne chahiye.

questions.question: A classmate says, 'I'm from Kochi.' Which reply best keeps the conversation going?
options: Oh, nice! What's it like living there?
questions.explanation: Open follow-up question saamne wale ko aur bolne ka mauka deta hai, isliye conversation chalti rehti hai. 'Okay' aur 'Hmm' baat khatam kar dete hain, aur last option topic ko rudely badal deta hai.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct in standard English for a self-introduction?
options: I am having two years of work experience.
I have two years of work experience.
I am knowing Python and SQL.
questions.explanation: 'have' yahan possession (state) dikhata hai, isliye simple present 'I have' sahi hai. 'am having' aur 'am knowing' stative verbs ka galat continuous use hai, aur 'Myself Rahul' standard introduction nahi hai.

questions.question: In a formal online interview, the interviewer says, 'Tell me about yourself.' Which opening is most appropriate?
options: Myself Anjali, I am from Lucknow only.
Good morning. I'm Anjali Verma, a first-year BS Data Science student from Lucknow.
Hi, what exactly do you want to know?
Everything is already written in my resume.
questions.explanation: Option 2 mein greeting, poora naam aur relevant background ek polite, formal tone mein hai. Option 1 mein 'Myself' aur 'only' Indianisms hain, option 3 casual aur defensive lagta hai, aur option 4 sawaal ko avoid karta hai.

weeks.title: Paragraphs and Emails
weeks.summary: Achha writing clear structure se aata hai. Is week aap topic sentence wala paragraph likhna, linkers use karna aur ek formal email ka sahi format seekhoge.
concepts: **Paragraph structure**: Topic sentence (main idea) + supporting sentences (reasons, examples) + concluding sentence (summary ya final thought).
**Unity**: Ek paragraph mein sirf ek main idea. Jo sentence topic se related nahi, use hata do.
**Coherence with linkers**: Ideas ko jodne ke liye: firstly, moreover (addition), however (contrast), therefore (result), for example, finally.
**Formal email parts**: Clear subject line, salutation (Dear Professor Iyer,), opening line mein purpose, short body, clear request, closing (Regards / Yours sincerely), aur poora naam.
**Subject line**: Specific aur short: 'Request for extension of Week 4 assignment deadline'. 'Hi' ya 'Urgent!!!' jaise vague subjects avoid karo.
**Formal tone**: 'Hey', 'plz', 'u', emojis aur ALL CAPS formal email mein nahi. Polite phrases: 'I would be grateful if...', 'Could you please...'.
**Revise before sending**: Spelling, grammar, attachments aur recipient ka naam ek baar check karo.

example.problem: Is informal message ko formal email mein badlo: 'hey sir plz extend deadline, was sick. thx'
steps: Subject line likho: 'Request for extension of assignment deadline due to illness'.
Salutation: 'Dear Sir,' (ya naam pata ho toh 'Dear Professor Rao,').
Opening mein purpose: 'I am writing to request a short extension for the Week 6 assignment.'
Reason politely: 'I was unwell for the past three days and could not complete it on time.'
Clear request: 'I would be grateful if you could allow me to submit it by Friday.'
Closing: 'Thank you for your understanding. Regards,' phir poora naam.
Answer: Ek structured email jismein subject, salutation, purpose, reason, request aur polite closing ho, bina 'hey', 'plz', 'thx' ke.

mistakes: Email mein subject line khaali chhodna ya 'Hi' likhna. Subject se hi reader ko pata chalna chahiye ki email kis baare mein hai.
Paragraph mein unrelated baatein daal dena. Har sentence ke baare mein poocho: kya yeh topic sentence ko support karta hai?
revision: Paragraph = topic sentence + support + conclusion.
Ek paragraph, ek idea (unity).
Linkers: moreover, however, therefore, for example.
Email: subject, salutation, purpose, body, request, closing, naam.
Formal email mein 'hey', 'plz', emojis nahi.

questions.question: Which is the best subject line for an email asking for more time to submit an assignment?
options: Request for extension of Week 4 assignment deadline
questions.explanation: Achha subject line specific hota hai aur reader ko bina email khole purpose bata deta hai. 'Hi', 'Urgent!!!' aur 'please read this' vague hain aur unprofessional lagte hain.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate salutation for an email to a professor whose name you know?
questions.explanation: Formal email mein 'Dear' + title + surname standard hai: 'Dear Professor Iyer,'. Baaki teeno bahut casual hain aur professor ke liye respectful nahi lagte.

questions.question: Which sentence works best as the topic sentence of a paragraph on the benefits of online learning?
options: I logged in at 7 p.m. yesterday.
Some lecture videos are twenty minutes long.
Online learning gives students flexibility in where and when they study.
In conclusion, that is all I have to say.
questions.explanation: Topic sentence paragraph ka main idea batata hai, aur option 3 seedha 'benefit' (flexibility) introduce karta hai. Options 1 aur 2 chhoti details hain, aur option 4 conclusion jaisa hai, opening nahi.

questions.question: I wanted to avoid last-minute stress. ___, I started the assignment a week early.
questions.explanation: Doosra sentence pehle sentence ka result hai (stress avoid karna tha, isliye jaldi shuru kiya), isliye 'Therefore'. 'However' contrast dikhata hai, aur 'Although' / 'Despite' sentence ke shuru mein is tarah comma ke saath akele nahi lagte.

questions.question: Which closing is most suitable for a formal email to a course instructor?
questions.explanation: 'Regards' ke saath poora naam ek safe, professional closing hai. 'Love' personal hai, 'Bye bye!' bolchaal wala hai, aur 'TTYL' chat ki short form hai jo formal email mein nahi chalti.

questions.question: A paragraph argues that students should sleep 7 to 8 hours before an exam. Which sentence does NOT belong in it?
options: Sleep helps the brain store what we studied during the day.
Many hostels serve breakfast at 7:30 a.m.
A tired mind makes more careless mistakes in calculations.
Students who rest well usually concentrate better in the exam hall.
questions.explanation: Hostel ke breakfast time ka neend aur exam performance se koi relation nahi hai, isliye yeh paragraph ki unity todta hai. Baaki teeno sentences seedhe 'neend kyun zaroori hai' ko support karte hain.
